steps: Check UT-AIR tags header_pressure_bar, compressor_current_a, and oil_temp_c prior to 2026-09-19T21:32:59Z: sustained high compressor current with dropping header pressure supports a severe compressed air leak or delivery failure, whereas high current with normal header pressure supports an unloader valve failure or mechanical dragging.

Check ST20-WLD tag air_pressure_bar and cycle_time_s leading up to the stop: pressure dropping below 5.3 bar supports local pneumatic starvation or weld cell actuator leak, while pressure within 5.3-5.9 bar refutes a local pressure deficit at ST20.

Check downstream ST30-WLD tag air_pressure_bar across the same time window: low pressure at ST30 supports a common plant-wide UT-AIR header supply drop, whereas normal ST30 pressure supports an isolated pneumatic leak or restriction at ST20.

Check ST20-WLD air_pressure_bar and UT-AIR header_pressure_bar for flatlined values, sudden drop to zero, or missing telemetry: flatline or instantaneous step drops support a failed pressure transmitter or wiring fault rather than a physical pneumatic leak.

Check UT-AIR maintenance and repair logs for recent work on compressor unloader valves, pressure regulators, or line filters: recent repairs support installation defects or sticking unloader mechanisms, while absence of work supports component degradation or pipe rupture.

A sustained fall in header pressure while the compressor runs loaded indicates demand exceeding supply, most often a distribution leak.

citations.quote: Regulated gun air (`air_pressure_bar`) normally sits at 5.6 bar within 5.3 to 5.9 bar. Below 5 bar the cell raises a low-air alarm; at 4.6 bar the supply-air interlock stops the cell. Gun force alarms (A-ST20-GUN-FRC, A-ST30-GUN-FRC) can appear as the air falls.

When gun air pressure falls at ST20 and ST30 together, the cause is upstream in the plant air supply; check the header pressure (see Section 6.2 of AM-CA-01 (Plant Air System and Utilities)) before working on either cell.
When gun air falls at one cell only, check that cell's filter-regulator, drop-leg ball valve and quick couplings.

| Gun air low at one cell only | Filter-regulator element clogged, regulator drifted, or local leak | Read the cell gauge; listen for leaks at the drop leg and couplings | Replace the filter element; reset the regulator; repair the leak |

Inspect flexible air hoses, quick-disconnect couplings, and joint fittings at identified leak points.
Replace worn or leaking pneumatic couplings, fittings, and damaged hose sections.
Re-pressurize the header and verify leak tightness and proper compressor load-unload cycling.
